selection_basis.rule: lexicographically smallest SHA256 digest among candidates tied at the maximum contrast score

anti_bias.exposure_note: Published H/Ru(0001) kinetic, barrier and quantum-tunneling information was encountered during candidate qualification. The defensible protection is prospective method/protocol freezing and post-freeze comparison, not a claim that literature outcomes were unknown.

primary_qualified_source.citation: McIntosh et al., Quantum Effects in the Diffusion of Hydrogen on Ru(0001), J. Phys. Chem. Lett. 4, 1565-1569 (2013)
primary_qualified_source.access: final published CC-BY article publicly accessible
evidence: He-3 spin-echo microscopic H diffusion from 75 to 250 K
nuclear quantum effects visible up to about 200 K
reported ab initio quantum treatment underestimates the low-temperature tunneling rate

quarantined_published_outcomes.purpose: may be retained as exposed literature evidence but cannot select the new electronic-structure method, convergence settings, path, quantum treatment, thresholds or dissipation model
fields: reported classical or zero-point-corrected diffusion barriers
reported experimental jump rates and Arrhenius parameters

why_this_is_a_limit_test: Hydrogen is a light nucleus for which nuclear quantum effects are experimentally important over the measured range.
A static classical barrier plus harmonic prefactor is therefore not presumed sufficient.

The published first-principles quantum calculation itself has a known low-temperature discrepancy, so the system is capable of rejecting an inadequate computational treatment rather than merely confirming a favorable case.
The substrate differs from Cu and the adsorbate class differs from both the Na development pilot and CO System 2.
reason_production_not_yet_authorized: The System 3 method and nuclear-quantum treatment must be frozen independently of the exposed kinetic outcomes, and generic Reaction-Path Engine contracts must be sufficiently separated from Na/Cu-specific assumptions before full production execution.
